At some instant the rod starts moving with a velocity $v_0$ along $X$-axis. The emf induced in the rod is

Now, induced emf (formula) E=B l v where, $B, l_{\perp}$ and $v$ are perpendicular to each other, $l=L / 2$ Now, consider a small element of length $d y$ at a distance $y$ from origin along $Y$-axis, then emf of element d E=B(d y) v_0=B_0 $\frac{y^3}{L^3}$v_0 $\cdot$d y Emf of the rod, $\begin{aligned}$& E=$\frac{B_0 v_0}{L^3} \int_0^{L / 2} y³ $\cdot$d y \\ \text{ and } E=$\frac{B_0 v_0}{L^3}\left\lceil\frac{y^4}{4}\right\rceil^{L / 2}$\\ \text{ and } E=$\frac{B_0 v_0}{L^3}\left\lfloor\frac{(L / 2)^4}{4}\right\rfloor \Rightarrow$E=$\frac{B_0 v_0 L}{64} \end{aligned}

questions.q: A rectangular loop of length $l$ and breadth $b$ is placed at distance of $x$ from infinitely long wire carrying current $i$ such that the direction of current is parallel to breadth. If the loop moves away from the current wire in a direction perpendicular to it with a velocity $v$, the magnitude of the emf in the loop is : ( $\mu_0=$ permeability of free space $)$
questions.solution:
We can show the situation as :
Since, loop is moving away from the wire, so the direction of current in the loop will be as shown in the figure. Net magnetic field on the loop due to wire $B=\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 \pi}\left(\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{l+x}\right)=\frac{\mu_0 i l}{2 \pi x(l+x)}$ So, the magnitude of the emf in the loop $e=v B b=\frac{\mu_0 \text { ilvb }}{2 \pi x(l+x)}$

questions.q: The endpoints of a conducting string (shaped as a circular loop) of constant length are being pulled at a constant velocity $v$ as shown in the figure. There exists a uniform magnetic field $B$ in space which is perpendicular to the circular loop. If the loop always remains circular during the motion of its endpoints, then the emf induced in the loop at $t = \dfrac{\piR}{2v}$ is
questions.solution:
At any instant, the radius of the loop $r$, will satisfy the following relation

$2\pir + 2vt = 2\piR$

$⇒ r = R - \dfrac{vt}{π}$

The flux of the magnetic field at any instant, will be

${ϕ}_{B} = \pir^{2}B$

So, the induced emf is

$Ε = \left|- \dfrac{d ϕ}{d t}\right| = 2\piBr\dfrac{d r}{d t}$

$⇒ Ε = 2\piB\left(R - \dfrac{vt}{π}\right)v$

$⇒ Ε = BRv$

$3 \times 10^{-3}=\frac{L}{R}3 \times 10^{-3}=\frac{L}{18}$
or $\quad L=54 \mathrm{mH}$

questions.solution: Given, frequency of revolution of the rod, $f=10 \mathrm{rev} / \mathrm{s}$, length of rod, $L=80 \mathrm{~cm}=0.8 \mathrm{~m}$ and magnetic field $B=0.5 \mathrm{~T}$ Since, rod is rotated about its mid point, hence radius of circular revolution, r=$\frac{L}{2}=\frac{0.8}{2}=$0.4 $\mathrm{~m}\therefore$ Potential difference between centre of rod and one end of rod due to revolution in magnetic is given by $\begin{aligned}$V^{\prime} & =$\text { induced emf }=\frac{\text { change in flux }}{\text { time taken }}$\\ $\frac{B . \pi r^2}{T}$& =B . $\pi$r^2 . f \quad  \left[\because$f=$\frac{1}{T}\right]$\\ & =0.5 $\times \pi \times($0.4)^2 $\times$10 \\ & =0.8 $\pi \end{aligned}\therefore$ Potential difference between two ends of rod due to revolution in the magnetic field, $V=2 V^{\prime}=2 \times 0.8 \pi=1.6 \pi$

questions.solution:
As, $I = \dfrac{E}{R} = \dfrac{dϕ}{Rdt}$
$⇒ Idt = \dfrac{dϕ}{R}$
Integrating,
$∫ Idt = ∫ \dfrac{dϕ}{R}$
$⇒ q = \dfrac{ϕ}{R}$
If coil contains $N$ turns, then $q = \dfrac{Nϕ}{R}$.
If there is flux change $\Deltaϕ$, then $q = \dfrac{N\Deltaϕ}{R}$.
$⇒ q = \dfrac{1}{7} \times \left(1.35 - 0.79\right) = 0.08C$

The axis of rotation is perpendicular to the field. If the total resistance of the circuit is $\text{R}$, the mean power generated per period of rotation is

Magnetic flux linked


$= \text{BA} \text\cos \omega t = \dfrac{\text{B} \pi r^{2} \text\cos \omega t}{2}$

$∴$ Induced emf $\text{e} = \dfrac{- \text{d} ϕ}{\text{dt}} = \dfrac{- 1}{2} \text{B} \pi r^{2} \omega \text\sin \omega t$

questions.q: Two long coaxial solenoids of radius $R$ and $2R$ have equal number of turns per unit length. They carry time-varying currents ${i}_{1} = 2kt$ and ${i}_{2} = kt$ respectively, in the same direction. A point charge released between the solenoids at a distance $r$, is seen to move along a circular path. Then the value of $r$ is
options: It can be any value between $R$ and $2R$
questions.solution:
The magnetic field due to the inner solenoid (within its volume) is

${B}_{1} = {μ}_{0}n \left(2kt\right)$

The magnetic field due to the outer solenoid (within its volume) is

${B}_{2} = {μ}_{0}n \left(kt\right)$

The flux of magnetic field through the circular area of radius $r$ is

$ϕ = {B}_{1}\piR^{2} + {B}_{2}\pir^{2}$

$⇒ ϕ = \pi{μ}_{0}nkt \left(2R^{2} + r^{2}\right)$

If $\overset{→}{E}$ is the induced electric field at $r$, then

$∮ \overset{→}{E} . d\overset{→}{r} = - $\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}

$⇒ E \times2\pir = \pi{μ}_{0}nk \left($2R^{2} + r^{2}\right)$

$⇒ E = {μ}_{0}nk \left(\dfrac{R2}{r} + \dfrac{r}{2}\right)$

The radius of the circle traversed by the charged particle is

$r = \dfrac{mv}{q{B}_{2}}$

$v = E\dfrac{qt}{m} = {μ}_{0}nk\left(\dfrac{R2}{r} + \dfrac{r}{2}\right)\dfrac{qt}{m}$

$⇒ {μ}_{0}nk\left(\dfrac{R2}{r} + \dfrac{r}{2}\right)\dfrac{qt}{m} = \dfrac{qr{B}_{2}}{m}$

$⇒ {μ}_{0}nkt\left(\dfrac{R2}{r} + \dfrac{r}{2}\right) =r{μ}_{0}nkt$

$⇒ R^{2} + \dfrac{r2}{2} =r^{2}$

$⇒ r = R\sqrt{2}$

$

questions.solution: Energy densities are $u_E=\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E^2$ u_B=$\frac{1}{2} \frac{B^2}{\mu_0}$So, energy required to setup a uniform electric field in cube of side $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ is $\begin{aligned}$U_E & =u_E $\times \text { Volume of cube }=\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E² $\times$l^3 \\  \text{ and }  =$\frac{1}{2} \times$8.9 $\times$10^{-12} $\times\left($10^7\right)^2 $\times($0.1)^3 \\  \text{ and }  =4.45 $\times$10^{-12+14-3} \\  \text{ and }  =4.45 $\times$10^{-1}=0.445 $\mathrm{~J} \end{aligned}$and energy required to setup a uniform magnetic field in cube of side $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ is $\begin{aligned}$U_B  \text{ and }  =u_B $\times \text { Volume of cube }$\\  \text{ and }  =$\frac{B^2 l^3}{2 \mu_0}=\frac{0.25 \times 0.25 \times(0.1)^3}{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 2}=$25 $\mathrm{~J} \end{aligned}

questions.q: A small square loop of wire of side $l$ is placed inside a large square loop of side $L(L>>l)$. If the loops are coplanar and their centres coincide, the mutual induction of the system is directly proportional to :
questions.solution:
Considering the larger loop to be made up of four rods each of length $L$, the field at the centre, i.e., at a distance \left(\frac{L}{2}\right)$ from each rod, will be
$B=4 \times \frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{l}{d}[\sin \alpha+\sin \beta]$ i.e., $\quad B=4 \times \frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{I}{\left(\frac{L}{2}\right)} \times 2 \sin 45$ i.e., $\quad B_1=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{8 \sqrt{2}}{L} I$ So, the flux with smaller loop $\phi_2=B_1 S_2=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{8 \sqrt{2}}{L} l^2 I$ and hence, $M=\frac{\phi_2}{I}=2 \sqrt{2} \frac{\mu_0}{\pi} \frac{l^2}{L}$ or $\quad M \propto \frac{l^2}{L}$

questions.solution: Given, $B=10^{-4} \mathrm{~T}, r=20 \mathrm{~cm}=20 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}\frac{d r}{d t}=-\frac{2 \mathrm{~mm}}{\mathrm{~s}}=-$2 \times 10^{-3} $\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s}}$Induced emf, $\varepsilon=-\frac{d \phi}{d t} \Rightarrow \varepsilon=-\frac{d}{d t} \left(B \cdot \pi r^2\right)\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } \varepsilon=-B \pi \cdot $\frac{d r^2}{d t}=-$B \pi  \left(2 r \cdot $\frac{d r}{d t}\right)\\ & \varepsilon=10^{-4} \times \pi \times 2 \times 20 \times 10^{-2} \times 2 \times 10^{-3} \\ & \varepsilon=8 \pi \times 10^{-8}=0.08 \pi(\mu \mathrm{V}) \end{aligned} $

questions.q: A square coil $ACDE$ with its plane vertical is released from rest in a horizontal uniform magnetic field $\overset{→}{B}$ which extends over a length $2L$ as shown in the figure. The acceleration of the coil is
options: less than $g$ for all the time till the loop crosses the magnetic field completely
less than $g$ when it enters the field and greater than $g$ when it comes out of the field
less than $g$ when it enters and comes out of the field but equal to $g$ when it is within the field
questions.solution:
There will be three situations,

(i) When the coil is entering into the field, flux increases and from Lenz's law the induced emf or current opposes the change. Therefore $a < g$ .

(ii) When the coil is completely within the field, flux remains constant and hence no emf is induced. Therefore $a = g$ .

(iii) When the coil is coming out from the field, flux decreases and from Lenz's law the induced emf or current opposes the change. Therefore $a < g$ .

questions.q: Find the potential difference between $a$ and $b$, as shown in the below circuit.
questions.solution:
Equivalent for parallel combination of& $5Ω \text{ and } 15Ω$~is~

${R}_{eq1} = \dfrac{15 \times 5}{15 + 5} = \dfrac{15}{4}Ω$

Similarly for three parallel resistor's equivalent~

$\dfrac{1}{Req2} = \dfrac{1}{24} + \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{8} ⇒ {R}_{eq2} = 4Ω$

Now current through~$45V$~branch,

$I = \dfrac{45}{Req1} = \dfrac{45}{15 / 4} = 12A$

Voltage across $a \text{ and } b$~is

$V = {R}_{eq} \times I = \left(4 + 10 + \dfrac{15}{4}\right) \times 12 = 213V$

questions.q: A long straight wire carrying current $I$ and a rectangular frame with side lengths $a$ and $b$ lie in the same plane as shown in the figure. The mutual inductance of the wire and frame is
questions.solution:
Magnetic field through the wire, $B=\frac{\mu_0 I b}{2 \pi a}$.
$\begin{array}{ll}\therefore \text { Magnetic flux induced, } \phi & =\oint_s \mathbf{B} \cdot d \mathbf{a} \\ \Rightarrow & \phi=\frac{\mu_0 I b}{2 \pi} \int_a^{a+a} \frac{d a}{a} \\ \Rightarrow & \phi=\frac{\mu_0 I b}{2 \pi} \ln 2\end{array} $\therefore$ Mutual inductance of the wire and the frame is M=\frac{\phi}{I}=\frac{\mu_0 b}{2 \pi} \ln2 $

questions.q: An artificial satellite with a metal surface is moving about the earth in a circular orbit. A current will be induced in the satellite, if&
options: the plane of the orbit coincides with the plane of the equator.
the plane of the orbit is inclined to the plane of the equator.
the plane of the orbit coincides with the plane of the equator and the speed of the satellite is more than $8km\sec^{- 1}$.
the plane of the orbit coincides with the plane of the equator and the speed of the satellite is less than $8km\sec^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, EMF will be generated across the ends of the conductor when the magnetic flux through a loop of the conductor will change with respect to time.

When the orbit of the satellite is inclined to the equator of the earth, the distance from poles and hence magnitude of the magnetic field due to earth will change at different positions of orbit.

This causes a change in magnetic flux across the metal plate of the satellite and EMF will be generated.

The voltage across an inductor is

$V = - L\dfrac{di}{dt}$

So the voltage across the inductor will always be opposite to the rate of change of current.

When $\dfrac{di}{dt} > 0$ then $V < 0$ and vice versa

Also, the magnitude of $V$ is proportional to the magnitude of $\dfrac{di}{dt}$.

When $\dfrac{di}{dt}$decreases, $V$ also decreases

questions.q: In the given electrical circuit, if the switch $S$ is closed then the maximum energy stored in the inductors is:
questions.solution:
In figure below, if switch $S$ is open then total energy stored in the capacitors, is suppose $E_0$.
Energy in IF capacitor, $E_1=\frac{1}{2}$C $V^2=\frac{1}{2}$C\$left(\frac{Q}{C}\r$right)^2=\frac{1}{2} \frac{Q^2}{C}=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4^2}{1}=$8 \mathrm{~J} Similarly, $E_2=\frac{1}{2} \frac{Q^2}{C}=\frac{2^2}{2 \times 2}=1 \mathrm{~J}$ So, the total energy, $E_0=E_1+E_2=8+1=9 \mathrm{~J}$ Now, switch's is closed then the common potential of Capacitors, $\begin{aligned}$V_{\text {common }} \text{ and } $=\frac{C_1 V_1+C_2 V_2}{C_1+C_2}$\\ \text{ and } $=\frac{1 \times 4+2 \times 1}{1+2}=\frac{6}{3}=$2 \mathrm{~V} \end{aligned} Hence, now the new arrangement of energy, and $\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } $E_1=\frac{1}{2}$C_1 V_{\text {common }}^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 4=2 \mathrm{~J} \\ \text{ and } $E_2=\frac{1}{2}$C_2 V_{\text {common }}^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 4=4 \mathrm{~J} \end{aligned} Now, from conservation of energy, Energy stored in the inductor, $E_L \simeq E_0- \left(E_1+E_2\right)$ =9-(2+4)=3 \mathrm{~J} Hence, the inductor has $3 \mathrm{~J} of energy.$

questions.q: Consider a toroid with rectangular cross section, of inner radius $a$, outer radius $b$ and height $h$, carrying $n$ number of turns. Then the self-inductance of the toroidal coil when current $I$ passing through the toroid is

Given, a toroid with a rectangular cross-section of inner radius $a$ and outer radius $b$. Height of the solenoid $=h$ Magnetic field inside a rectangular toroid is given by $B=\frac{\mu_0 n I}{2 \pi r}$
using the infinitesimal cross-sectional area element, $d x=h d r\therefore$ Flux passing through the cross-section of toroid. $\begin{aligned} \phi & =\int B \cdot d x=\int_a^b \frac{\mu_0 n I}{2 \pi r} \cdot(h d r) \\ & \phi=\frac{\mu_0 n I h}{2 \pi} \int_a^b \frac{1}{r} d r \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \phi=\frac{\mu_0 n h I}{2 \pi}\left[\log r l_a^b\right. \\ \phi & =\frac{\mu_0 n h I}{2 \pi}(\log b-\log a) \\ & \phi=\frac{\mu_0 n h I}{2 \pi} \ln \left(\frac{b}{a}\right)\end{aligned}$ Now, self inductance of rectangular toroid, $L=\frac{n \phi}{I}$ Putting the value of $\phi$, we get $L=\frac{\mu n^2 h}{2 \pi} \ln $\$left(\frac{b}{a}\right)

questions.q: A long solenoid of cross-sectional radius $R$ has a thin insulated wire ring of uniform cross-section tightly put on its winding. The ring is made out of two different material such that one half of the ring has a resistance $10$ times that of the other half. The magnetic induction produced by the solenoid varies with time as $B = bt$, where $b$ is a constant. The magnitude of the electric field strength in the ring (other than the induced electric field) is
questions.solution:
Let us assume that the current in the ring is $i$ and the resistance of the two halves are $r$ and $10r$, then by faraday's law

\left|\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}\right| = \piR^{2}b = ir + i\left(10r\right)$

$⇒ i = \dfrac{\piR^{2}b}{11r}$

The induced electric field in both the parts of the ring is

${E}_{ind} = \dfrac{R}{2}\dfrac{dB}{dt} = \dfrac{Rb}{2}$



Let $E$ be the field which is developed in each part due to charge accumulation at the junctions, then for the upper half

\left({E}_{ind} + E\right)\piR = i \left(10r\right)$

and for the lower half

\left({E}_{ind} -E\right)\piR = ir$

$⇒ 2E\piR - 9ir = 0$

$E = $\dfrac{9ir}{2\piR}

$⇒ E = $\dfrac{9r}{2\piR} \times \dfrac{\piR^{2}b}{11r} = \dfrac{9}{22}$Rb$

$

case~$i$~: for~$0 ° to90 °$~position

case~$ii$~: for~$90 ° to180 °$~position

questions.q: A magnetic field given by $B(t)=\left(0.2 t-0.05 t^2\right) T$ is directed perpendicular to the plane of a circular coil containing 25 turns of radius $1.8 \mathrm{~cm}$ and whose total resistance is $5 \Omega$. The power dissipation at $3 \mathrm{~s}$ is nearly
questions.solution: Given that, number of turns, $N=25$ Radius of coil, $r=1.8 \mathrm{~cm}=1.8 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}$ Resistance of coil, $R=5 \Omega$ Magnetic field, $B=\left(0.2 t-0.05 t^2\right) \mathrm{T}$ Now, area of coil, $\begin{aligned} A & =\pi r^2=3.14 \times\left(1.8 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ & =1.02 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}$ Induced emf, $\varepsilon=\frac{-N d}{d t}(B A)=-N A \frac{d B}{d t}\begin{aligned} & =-N A \frac{d}{d t}\left(0.2 t-0.05 t^2\right) \\ \varepsilon & =-N A(0.2-0.1 t)\end{aligned}$ Substituting the values, we get $\begin{aligned} \varepsilon & =-25 \times 1.02 \times 10^{-3}(0.2-0.1 t) \\ & =-2.55 \times 10^{-2}(0.2-0.1 t)\end{aligned}$ Now, instantaneous power, $P=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{R}=\frac{\left[-2.55 \times 10^{-2}(0.2-0.1 t)\right]^2}{5}$ At, $t=3 \mathrm{~s}$, power dissipated is $P=\frac{\left(2.55 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2(0.2-0.1 \times 3)^2}{5}=1.30 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~W}=1.30 \mu \mathrm{W}$ It is close to option (d).
